name: AD9834BRUZ-REEL
title: AD9834: 75 MHz low-power DDS with 10-bit DAC, comparator and 3-wire serial interface, 2.3 V to 5.5 V, TSSOP-20
summary: A direct digital synthesizer: a 28-bit phase accumulator, two frequency and two phase registers, a sine look-up and a 10-bit current-output DAC give sine or triangle waves up to 37.5 MHz from a clock of up to 75 MHz. An on-chip comparator squares up the filtered output for clock generation, or the NCO MSB can be sent out directly. It is programmed with 16-bit words over a 3-wire serial port clocked up to 40 MHz, and FSELECT and PSELECT pins switch registers for FSK and PSK. Analog and digital supplies are separate, each 2.3 V to 5.5 V, at about 20 mW from 3 V; grade B runs to 50 MHz MCLK and grade C to 75 MHz.

pins.name: FS ADJUST
pins.function: Full-scale adjust. A resistor RSET from this pin to AGND sets the full-scale DAC current: IOUT FULL SCALE = 18 × FSADJUST / RSET, with FSADJUST 1.15 V nominal and RSET 6.8 kΩ typical.

pins.name: REFOUT
pins.function: Output of the internal 1.20 V voltage reference.

pins.name: COMP
pins.function: DAC bias node, brought out for its decoupling capacitor.

pins.name: AVDD
pins.function: Analog supply, 2.3 V to 5.5 V. Decouple to AGND with 0.1 µF.

pins.name: DVDD
pins.function: Digital supply, 2.3 V to 5.5 V. Decouple to DGND with 0.1 µF.

pins.name: CAP/2.5V
pins.function: Output of the on-chip regulator that makes the 2.5 V core supply from DVDD when DVDD is above 2.7 V; it takes a decoupling capacitor to DGND, typically 100 nF. With DVDD at 2.7 V or below, short this pin to DVDD.

pins.name: DGND
pins.function: Digital ground.

pins.name: MCLK
pins.function: Master clock input. The output frequency is a binary fraction of MCLK, and its accuracy and phase noise follow this clock.

pins.name: FSELECT
pins.function: Frequency select: chooses FREQ0 or FREQ1 for the phase accumulator. When the FSEL bit does the choosing, hold this pin at a CMOS high or low.

pins.name: PSELECT
pins.function: Phase select: chooses whether PHASE0 or PHASE1 is added to the accumulator output. When the PSEL bit does the choosing, hold this pin at a CMOS high or low.

pins.name: RESET
pins.function: Active high. Clears the relevant internal registers to zero, giving a midscale analog output; the addressable registers keep their contents.

pins.name: SLEEP
pins.function: Active high. While high, the DAC is powered down; the same action as control bit SLEEP12.

pins.name: SDATA
pins.function: Serial data input for the 16-bit word.

pins.name: SCLK
pins.function: Serial clock input; data is taken in on each falling edge.

pins.name: FSYNC
pins.function: Active low frame sync for the serial input; taking it low tells the logic a new word is coming.

pins.name: SIGN BIT OUT
pins.function: Logic output carrying either the comparator output or the NCO MSB. Enabled by bit OPBITEN = 1; bit SIGN/PIB picks which signal.

pins.name: VIN
pins.function: Comparator input. With OPBITEN and SIGN/PIB both 1 the comparator takes its input from this pin; filtering the DAC output before it reaches this pin lowers jitter on the square wave.

pins.name: AGND
pins.function: Analog ground.

pins.name: IOUT
pins.function: High-impedance DAC current output. Load it with a 200 Ω resistor (nominal) to AGND; 20 pF to AGND is also recommended against clock feedthrough.

pins.name: IOUTB
pins.function: Complementary DAC current output. Preferably loaded with 200 Ω to AGND, though it may go straight to AGND; 20 pF to AGND is also recommended against clock feedthrough.

circuits.title: Test circuit for the specifications
circuits.description: The load and decoupling under which the specifications are measured. RSET of 6.8 kΩ on FS ADJUST sets about 3 mA full scale; IOUT drives a 200 Ω load with 20 pF across it. The regulator output CAP/2.5V has 100 nF to ground, REFOUT has 10 nF, and the DAC bias pin COMP has 10 nF to AVDD.

circuits.title: ADSP-21xx to AD9834 interface
circuits.description: A serial-port DSP writes the AD9834 directly: its transmit frame sync drives FSYNC, DT carries the data and its serial clock drives SCLK. The SPORT runs in transmit alternate framing mode (TFSW = 1) with internal clock (ISCLK = 1), active-low framing (INVTFS = 1), 16-bit words (SLEN = 15), internal frame sync (ITFS = 1) and one frame sync per write (TFSR = 1). Data leaves on rising SCLK edges and is taken in on falling edges.

circuits.title: 68HC11/68L11 to AD9834 interface
circuits.description: The microcontroller is SPI master (MSTR = 1 in SPCR): SCK drives SCLK and MOSI drives SDATA, while port line PC7 serves as FSYNC because the SPI has no frame-sync pin. Settings: CPOL = 0 with SCK idling high between writes, CPHA = 1 so data is valid on the falling edge. Each 16-bit word goes as two bytes, MSB first; PC7 stays low across both and returns high only after the second byte.

circuits.title: 80C51/80L51 to AD9834 interface
circuits.description: The controller's serial port runs in Mode 0: TXD clocks SCLK, RXD carries SDATA, and port pin P3.3 is FSYNC. A word is sent as two bytes with P3.3 held low throughout and raised after the second; SCLK idles high between the two. The port shifts out LSB first while the AD9834 expects MSB first, so the software reverses each byte's bit order before sending.

circuits.title: DSP56002 to AD9834 interface
circuits.description: The DSP's SSI is set for normal mode, asynchronous, gated internal clock (SYN = 0, GCK = 1, SCKD = 1), an internally generated frame sync on SC2 (SC2 = 1), 16-bit words (WL1 = 1, WL0 = 0) and a frame sync spanning the word (FSL = 0). SC2 has the wrong sense for FSYNC, so an inverter sits between them; STD drives SDATA and SCK drives SCLK. The DSP56000 and DSP56001 connect the same way.

operation.text: A 28-bit phase accumulator, fed from FREQ0 or FREQ1, forms the numerically controlled oscillator. One of two 12-bit phase registers is added to its top bits, the sum is cut to 12 bits and addressed into the SIN ROM, and a 10-bit current DAC turns the result into IOUT and IOUTB. Twelve bits of phase are kept so that truncation error stays below one DAC LSB. Switching frequency register keeps the phase continuous. Apart from the chip, a complete sine source up to 37.5 MHz takes a clock, a single low-precision resistor and eight decoupling capacitors.

The DAC is a high-impedance current source, usable single-ended or differentially: equal resistors from IOUT and IOUTB to AGND give complementary voltages. Any load value works if the full-scale voltage across it stays inside the compliance range; RSET can be changed to offset a change in load. MODE = 0 gives a sine, MODE = 1 bypasses the SIN ROM and gives a 10-bit linear triangle. SLEEP and SLEEP12 must both be 0 whenever IOUT and IOUTB are used.

The full-scale current set by RSET is at most 4 mA. The output may rise to VDD − 1.5 V, 0.8 V at a 2.3 V supply; above that the internal switch's impedance shifts and spectral performance suffers. The specifications hold for RSET = 6.8 kΩ and RLOAD = 200 Ω.

Being sampled, the output carries images around every multiple of MCLK (fC ± fOUT, 2fC ± fOUT and so on) under a sin(x)/x envelope; how strong they are depends on the ratio of fOUT to MCLK, and the first image can come within about 3 dB of the fundamental. A low-pass filter usually sits between the DAC and the comparator. For a clock generator, keeping fOUT below 33% of MCLK keeps images away from the wanted band and makes the filter simpler.

The on-chip comparator is self-biasing and ac-coupled: its threshold is the average of the signal at VIN. It takes about 100 mV p-p to 1 V p-p and needs at least about 3 MHz input to act as a zero-crossing detector. Its square-wave output swings 0 V to DVDD at SIGN BIT OUT. It is turned on by setting SIGN/PIB and OPBITEN to 1.

AVDD and DVDD are separate and independent, each 2.3 V to 5.5 V; one may be 5 V while the other is 3 V. The core runs at 2.5 V from an on-chip regulator fed by DVDD; the serial port runs from DVDD and is level shifted inside. At DVDD of 2.7 V or less, tie CAP/2.5V to DVDD to bypass the regulator.

Three wires, compatible with SPI, QSPI, MICROWIRE and DSP ports, clock up to 40 MHz. Words are 16 bits. FSYNC is level triggered and acts as both frame sync and chip enable: after it goes low (respecting t7), data shifts in on 16 falling SCLK edges, and FSYNC may rise after the 16th (respecting t8). FSYNC may instead stay low across a multiple of 16 clocks to stream words, rising after the last. SCLK may run continuously or idle high or low, but must be high when FSYNC falls (t12).

Reset the part at power-up and hold RESET at 1 until output is wanted, so the DAC makes no spurious output while the registers are loaded. RESET leaves the frequency, phase and control registers alone, and they power up holding invalid data, so write them all. Then return RESET to 0; the DAC output follows eight MCLK cycles later.

RESET clears the relevant internal registers to give a midscale output, without touching the frequency, phase or control registers. The RESET pin acts when PIN/SW = 1 and the RESET bit when PIN/SW = 0. Raising RESET acts at the output immediately; its falling edge is read on an internal falling MCLK edge, and the DAC output resumes seven MCLK cycles after RESET goes back to 0.

FSELECT and PSELECT take eight MCLK cycles to act when t11 and t11A are met, one more when they are not. A write to the selected frequency or phase register reaches the output after eight to nine MCLK cycles, the one-cycle spread depending on where the MCLK rising edge falls. The falling edges of RESET and SLEEP are sampled on the internal falling edge of MCLK, so they also have latency; their rising edges act at once, unsampled.

DB15 and DB14 address each word: 00 control register, 01 FREQ0, 10 FREQ1, 11 a phase register (DB13 picks PHASE0 or PHASE1, DB12 is don't-care, DB11 to DB0 the phase). With B28 = 1 a frequency register takes two consecutive writes, LSBs then MSBs. With B28 = 0, HLB chooses which 14-bit half a single write changes, for coarse tuning (MSBs) or fine tuning (LSBs). Repeated writes to one frequency register cause intermediate updates, so for a sweep alternate between the two registers.

PIN/SW = 1 hands frequency and phase register selection to the FSELECT and PSELECT pins; PIN/SW = 0 hands it to the FSEL and PSEL bits, and the pins should then sit at a CMOS level. Control can move between pins and bits freely. The pins are sampled on the internal falling edge of MCLK; a change at that edge leaves one cycle of uncertainty in when the switch happens.

The internal clock and the DAC can be shut down. With SLEEP1 = 1 the MCLK is gated off inside, the NCO stops and the DAC holds its value; registers can still be written and selected, and changes appear after the usual latency once SLEEP1 returns to 0. Powering the DAC down (SLEEP pin or SLEEP12) saves current when only the MSB output at SIGN BIT OUT is used.

The pin must be enabled with OPBITEN = 1, and MODE must then be 0. It carries either the comparator output (SIGN/PIB = 1) or the NCO MSB (SIGN/PIB = 0), the MSB being a coarse clock that DIV2 can halve.

Modulation is done in the digital domain. For FSK the two frequency registers hold the mark and space frequencies and the data stream drives FSELECT. The two phase registers allow PSK. GMSK and QPSK can also be built. The low current suits local-oscillator use, and the comparator lets the part make square waves for signal generation.

Keep analog and digital sections in separate board areas with ground planes joined at one point only; if the AD9834 is the only part needing the join, make it at its AGND and DGND pins, otherwise at a star point close to the part. Run the analog ground plane under the part and keep digital lines out from under it. Use wide supply tracks, shield fast clocks with digital ground, avoid analog and digital crossovers, and run traces on opposite sides at right angles. Decouple each supply to its ground with 0.1 µF ceramic in parallel with 10 µF tantalum, as close to the pins as possible. With one shared supply, use the system AVDD rail for both pins, each with its own decoupling. For the comparator, keep VIN and SIGN BIT OUT apart with a ground plane between them, for instance on opposite outer layers of a multilayer board.
